Subject: Pricing questions for Redwood Order Form

Hi Neha / Derek,

Thanks for sending the order form draft. Our procurement team reviewed the pricing exhibit and has a couple of open items:

- Annual minimum / floor: the exhibit shows a $250k annual minimum. Can you confirm whether that is a hard floor or if it can be graduated in year 1?
- Caps on overage: we need a hard cap on monthly overage charges for burst months. Would Redwood accept a monthly cap tied to 150% of committed spend?
- Discounts & renewal: we expect any tiered discount to persist into renewal unless mutually renegotiated. Is that standard for Redwood?

I've attached our internal PO stub for reference. Derek, looping legal to see if they want to redline the pricing exhibit directly.

Thanks,

Hi Megan — appreciate the clear list. Short answers:

- Annual minimums are configurable for enterprise deals; we can propose a graduated schedule for year 1.
- We can contractually limit overage exposure; need to define whether that cap applies per-month or per-billing-year and how it interacts with burst capacity.
- Discount tiers are typically tied to committed spend and applied at invoice time; renewals are negotiable but discounts do not automatically increase unless specified in the order form.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call to walk through the exact language (caps vs. floors) tomorrow? I've attached a slightly edited order form that shows where we usually capture the 'Annual Minimum Commitment' and 'Overage Cap' language.

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines

Thanks for the redline, Derek. A couple of suggestions from sales/ops to keep the economics predictable and implementable:

- Define the Cap as a monthly token spend cap per billing period (e.g., "Cap Amount" = 150% of the Monthly Committed Token Spend). That keeps billing deterministic and avoids cross-month pooling ambiguity.
- For the Annual Minimum, consider: Year 1 = 75% of listed Annual Commitment, Year 2 = 100%. We can show a stepped table in the exhibit to make invoicing straightforward.
- For Burst Capacity, add language that burst usage above the committed amount will be invoiced at the overage rate up to the Cap Amount; beyond the Cap Amount, Redwood will throttle non-critical burst traffic (or route to best-effort capacity) — we can add an SLA carve-out for capped months.

Attaching a draft pricing schedule with our suggested contract language. If legal is comfortable, we can incorporate these as counters.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_schedule_redline_from_redwood.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 28 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: contracts@acmecloud.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines (internal legal counter)

Team — filing a quick internal counter-proposal for Acme's redline. Notes:

- We support a graduated Annual Minimum for onboarding risk mitigation. Proposed language: "Year 1 Minimum = 75% of Annual Commitment; Year 2 Minimum = 100% of Annual Commitment."
- Concern: a hard monthly cap at 150% could hurt availability for mission-critical burst events. Suggest we offer a capped invoiced exposure of 150% but retain the right to allow overage beyond the cap on a best-effort basis (documented as "Excess Burst, Best Effort") so Acme isn't cut off mid-critical-incident.
- Discounts: clarify that quoted discounts apply to committed spend and overages billed at standard overage rate unless otherwise specified.

If everyone agrees, Neha can send this as Redwood's formal counter to Acme. I added a redline doc with tracked changes.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing exhibit — caps & floors redline

Thanks — this read-through is helpful and aligns with what procurement and legal discussed. Acme can accept:

- Year 1 at 75% floor, Year 2 at 100%.
- Monthly Cap Amount defined as 150% of Monthly Committed Token Spend for invoicing protection.
- Agreement that Redwood will make reasonable efforts to serve burst usage beyond the cap but invoicing exposure will be limited to the Cap Amount (we understand the carve-out language you proposed).

One remaining ask: can Redwood confirm whether the discount tier applied to committed spend will be preserved (at the same discount rate) if Acme achieves higher commit mid-contract, or will that only apply at renewal? We'd like the order form to include a short clause that if customer achieves higher committed spend during the term, the higher tier discount will apply prospectively to invoice periods after the tier is hit.

If you can incorporate that clause and send a final redline, we'll route to procurement and legal for signature.

Best,
Megan Ortiz
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Cloud
